notes.title: Paired insects beside the warning
notes.text: Two upright insect-like figures flank the middle of the text, with their heads above long striped wings. They face inward toward the text. Compare the paired figures below the text on LP1-15; the placement differs, and no exact source-image reuse is established.

notes.title: Curled borders and central ornaments

Separate ornaments sit above and below the text, each combining a central filled dot, outlined shapes and two curled arms. Similarity of the upper and lower arrangements does not by itself establish an exact geometric transformation.

notes.title: Red heading and red closing phrase
notes.text: The warning opens with an enlarged red initial and smaller red runes. Near the end, red text begins partway through the penultimate row and continues on the final row, followed by a red punctuation cluster. The known reading gives FOR ALL IS SACRED for this closing phrase. These visible red runes are separate from the JPEG’s extracted OutGuess payload.

notes.title: Leafy border around the Welcome text
notes.text: Thick curving branches surround the central text column. Dense leaf-shaped forms occupy the top, while larger open loops and scattered leaves descend along both margins and curve beneath the text. LP1-03 and LP1-04 share this broad arrangement. It is distinct from the narrow single-margin branching drawings on LP2-08 through LP2-14; no plant species or cipher operation is established by the resemblance.

Keeping the numbers and replacing each word with its additive Gematria Primus value produces a square whose rows, columns and both main diagonals sum to 1033. The original tokens are not all identical under a half-turn even though their converted values are. The magic-square guide records every substitution.

notes.text: Long black stems frame both sides of the text, combining large curls with smaller curled branches and root-like ends. A hanging cluster of thin branches occupies the middle of each border. The resemblance between the margins is visible; an exact reflection or reuse of the same source image has not been established by this observation.

notes.title: Left border: solid marks and pale rings
notes.text: The left cluster contains three solid black marks and two pale outlined rings. The outlines are much fainter than the solid marks, so a dark-pixel threshold can omit them. Inspect the original colors before treating all five positions as equivalent.

notes.title: Right border: five solid marks
notes.text: The right cluster contains five solid black marks. Compare its fill with the left cluster on this same page. The difference is visible; a binary encoding or a numerical meaning has not been established.

notes.title: Red opening beside three rows
notes.text: An enlarged red opening rune extends alongside the first three text rows. Smaller red runes follow on the first row, ending at a compact red punctuation cluster before black text continues. The pale tree and winged figure associated with this two-page community group appear on LP2-55, not on this page.

notes.title: Pale tree above a winged figure
notes.text: A pale gray, tree-shaped outline lies between the short text block and a dark winged figure at the bottom. The tree and insect-like figure are separate visible elements. The tree has branching contours and a trunk-like base; its intended meaning and source are not established.

notes.title: Winged figure and curled borders
notes.text: The lower figure has outspread wings with dark internal detail. Curled, branching borders run down the left and right margins. Compare the layout with LP2-53, keeping the added tree and the different amount of text in view.

notes.title: Red dotted mark at the end of the text
notes.text: A narrow red cluster of small square marks follows the final black runes. Compare its visible layout with the closing clusters on LP2-22 and the other illustrated tree page. Similar appearance and placement do not by themselves establish a cipher reset or a shared meaning.

notes.title: Five large black dots below the text
notes.text: Five filled black dots form a loose arrangement below the final two runic rows. They are much larger than the small red punctuation clusters within the text. This is another five-dot arrangement to compare with LP2-07 and LP2-23; the count alone does not identify a symbol, reading order or decoding instruction.

notes.title: Hexadecimal block between runic passages
notes.text: Five rows of Latin hexadecimal characters sit between an upper runic passage and two lower runic rows. The characters are printed directly on the page. The target guide joins those rows into one 128-character string while retaining their original display breaks.

notes.title: Red opening and small red closing marks
notes.text: An enlarged red initial stands beside the upper passage, with smaller red runes on its first row. Small red punctuation clusters close the upper and lower runic passages. The large black dots farther below are a separate visual feature.

notes.title: Stippled insect-like figure
notes.text: Below the final parable is a figure formed from many small black marks. A dense central body extends downward, with scattered marks spreading into wing-like areas on both sides. This rendering differs from the outlined and shaded winged figures on LP2-53 and LP2-55.

notes.title: Red opening and punctuation
notes.text: The text begins with an enlarged red rune beside the first three rows and smaller red runes on the opening row. Red punctuation clusters also appear in the text. Their visual color should be kept separate from the rune-only prime sums calculated from the known reading.
